subject: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

Hi Marcus + Aisha,

We’re getting pulled into a few enterprise security reviews this week (EU-only processing + audit evidence). I want to align on:

1) Beta scope: what we’re committing to for Hosted and Dedicated in Beta (and what we’re explicitly NOT).
2) Exception policy: whether we allow any cross-region fallback during capacity incidents, and how we document it.
3) Customer messaging: how we explain denial behavior + how customers should configure endpoints/SDKs.

Can you both sanity-check the following positions? (Draft attached)

Proposed Beta commitments:
- Hosted + Dedicated: region pinning at org/project, enforced at request admission (gateway) BEFORE model execution.
- No implicit cross-region fallback when pinned.
- On violation: return deterministic error with machine-readable code + emit audit event.
- Downstream writes: ensure audit logs + traces + analytics writes stay in-region (or fail closed + log).

Proposed Beta non-goals:
- No auto-migration of existing stored artifacts.
- No guarantee that historical logs are fully region-consolidated (separate retention/migration workstream).

Exception question:
- Do we support a time-boxed “allow_cross_region_fallback” override for true incident scenarios? If yes, needs GRC evidence + explicit opt-in + expiry.

I’d love an answer by EOD, since Marissa is pushing a customer-facing beta email tomorrow.

Thanks,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Residency_Enforcement_Beta_Scope_v0.9.docx


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

Naomi — overall +1 on the Beta commitments.

Security POV on exceptions:
- Default should be STRICT: pinned means pinned; no automatic fallback.
- If we add an override, it must be:
  a) explicit per-org setting (not per-request),
  b) time-bounded with an expiry date,
  c) auditable (who/when/why),
  d) surfaced in Console as “Residency exception active”,
  e) emits audit events on each cross-region routing decision.

Two concerns:
1) “Incident toggle” is often treated like a convenience toggle. We need an approval trail and constraints.
2) We should avoid wording that sounds like we’re guaranteeing continuity of service at the expense of residency. It should be framed as customer-controlled exception.

Olga: can you confirm what fields you need on the audit side for evidence?

- Marcus


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:26 AM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

Agree with Marcus. For leadership context: we should not create a “fail open” default that undermines the entire premise.

I’m comfortable with a tightly governed exception path, but it has to be framed as:
- customer-requested, documented, time-limited,
- not enabled by support during an incident without approval,
- and not marketed as a standard operating mode.

Also, please ensure the customer messaging includes clear guidance like:
- “Use the EU base URL / region setting; do not hardcode US endpoints.”
- “If you attempt to send traffic to a non-approved region, we will deny the request before processing and return a remediation link.”

Thanks for driving this.

Aisha


From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:02 PM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

For evidence, we need consistent audit events on:
1) policy evaluation (allow/deny + which policy applied), and
2) any exception activation/deactivation.

Minimum fields we should treat as non-negotiable:
- org_id / project_id (or stable tenant identifiers)
- request_id / trace_id (so customers can correlate)
- evaluated_region + pinned/allowed regions
- decision (allow/deny) + reason_code
- actor + actor_type for config changes (admin user vs system)
- exception_id (if applicable) + expiry

If we do a template for exceptions, I’d like to standardize “business justification” and “customer acknowledgement” language.

I can provide a draft form today.

- Olga


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:19 PM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

Looping in Nikhil + Marissa since this impacts customer comms and docs.

Decision direction (unless anyone objects):
- Beta = strict enforcement when pinned.
- No automatic cross-region fallback.
- Optional exception: time-boxed org-level “allow_cross_region_fallback” (explicit opt-in, approval trail, audit events per decision).

Nikhil: can you make sure Hosted docs/quickstarts don’t accidentally steer customers to the wrong base URL? We’re seeing a lot of “copy/paste US endpoint” in the wild.

Marissa: for the beta email, please use the “customer-controlled exception” framing and avoid any language that implies we might silently process out of region.

Also: we should be very clear that when pinned, requests sent to non-approved region are denied at admission (before inference).

- Naomi


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:07 AM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

Thanks. Drafting the beta announcement now.

Two questions for final copy:
1) What do we call this in the product? “Region pinning” vs “Data residency enforcement”? (I prefer the latter but it might imply more than we’re doing in beta.)
2) For error messaging: do we want to provide the remediation steps in-line (change base URL / SDK region) AND link to docs?

Also attaching draft messaging for review.

Attachment: Customer_Messaging_Data_Residency_Beta_v3.md


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:38 AM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

On naming: recommend “Region pinning (Data residency enforcement)” for beta.

We’ve had confusion historically where “data residency” implies storage migration + all artifacts. Beta isn’t that.

For comms, a short FAQ block helps:
- what is enforced now (request processing + in-scope logging paths)
- what isn’t yet (historical data + automatic migration)
- how to enable
- what happens on violations (deny + audit)

- Connor


From: Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 2:16 PM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

Adding reliability angle:
- The “no cross-region fallback when pinned” constraint will increase hard-denies during regional capacity events unless we size Dedicated correctly.
- That’s okay as long as we set expectation: pinned residency trades availability for residency guarantees.

If we permit a fallback exception, make sure it’s not an SRE “break glass” that bypasses approval. We can still have an operational playbook that routes customers to request the exception.

Also, I’d like a single sentence in customer messaging: “When pinned, we do not automatically fail over to another region.” That clarity saves us.

- Miles


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Miles Thornton <miles.thornton@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 5:48 PM
Subject: Re: Beta scope + exception policy for Hosted Data Residency enforcement

Thanks all — I’m going to lock decisions so teams can ship and Sales/Support can message consistently.

Final decisions for Beta:

Naming:
- “Region pinning (data residency enforcement)” in customer-facing materials.
- Internally, we can keep the initiative title “Hosted data residency enforcement.”

Behavior (Pinned):
- Enforced at request admission (gateway) before model execution.
- No implicit cross-region fallback when pinned.
- Violations return clear error (HTTP + error_code) with remediation guidance + docs link.

Exception policy:
- We will support a time-boxed org-level exception to allow cross-region fallback ONLY if:
  1) customer requests/acknowledges,
  2) Security + GRC approval recorded,
  3) expiry is set (max 7 days for beta; revisit at GA),
  4) every cross-region routing decision emits an audit event.
- Not available as a Support/SRE “toggle” without approvals.

Olga: please circulate the exception request template when ready; I’ll route for signoff.
Marissa: your draft looks good—please incorporate the naming and one-line “no automatic failover” sentence.
Nikhil: please add a prominent “choose your base URL/region” callout in Hosted quickstart.

If anyone sees issues with this framing, reply tonight; otherwise we’ll proceed.

- Naomi

Attachment: Exception_Request_Template_v1.pdf
